summary: A funded collar is not possible for CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives or their Associates: para 9 bans any transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to any vested Group Securities, and para 16(a) bans using Group Securities as security for margin lending or any other secured financing. For other Specified Persons (e.g. Executive General Managers, Subsidiary Board directors, Group Control Room staff), the hedge leg over vested shares free of any holding lock is not expressly banned, but the OTC options are Securities and entering them is a Trade, so it must be done in a Trading Window, with Pre-Clearance where designated on the Conflicts Hub (valid three business days), subject to the 30-day LIFO holding rule, and it must not involve CFDs, short selling or stock lending of Group Securities. The loan leg secured on the collared shares is prohibited for all Specified Persons, so at most an unsecured or unfunded collar is workable for that group, and exercise or settlement mechanics that execute outside a Trading Window are a further risk under para 11. Employees who are not Specified Persons face only the insider trading prohibition and whatever Pre-Clearance the unpublished Procedure imposes. The MAR overlay in para 18 adds an outright bar for the senior group on any Security that prices off a UK/EU-listed Group Security.

summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is a short 2011 insider-trading document with no substantive prohibitions on hedging, derivatives, margin lending or secured financing. Both collar legs are PME Securities because the definition expressly captures equity swaps, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, cash-settled or not, so entering, rolling, unwinding and settling the collar are each Dealings that require prior written notice of intention to the Company Secretary, a written confirmation of no Inside Information, and advice from the Company Secretary that there is no known reason to preclude the Dealing, with execution inside 7 days. Dealings must fall within one of the three 30-day Trading Windows after the full-year results, half-year results and AGM, outside the two four-week Blackout Periods and any ad hoc Blackout the Board or Chairman declares, and the Chairman may shorten a window or bar an individual; out-of-window execution needs the Chairman's (or for the Chairman, the Board's) approval on exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship, subject to any conditions including disclosure. The secured loan is not itself a Dealing and is not prohibited, but full details of any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting the shares must be reported in writing to the Company Secretary after the Dealing, and directors must also meet their notifiable interest obligations and their letter agreement with the company. The main residual risks are the narrow dealing calendar with no forced-sale carve-out, and the rules of the Pro Medicus Share and Option Plans, which are incorporated by reference and may impose hedging or encumbrance restrictions on plan shares that this policy does not.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for IAG Specified Persons, the population that includes the directors and executives a bank would target. Clause 34, added by the 30 November 2023 amendment, prohibits Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties from using IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, with margin lending and transfers into a margin account given only as examples, and no approver has power to waive it. The derivative legs alone are also constrained: instruments that limit economic risk are themselves IAG Securities, so entry, roll and unwind each require a Trading Consent Request approved by the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary (or, for Non-Executive Directors, the more senior approver route), inside one of the three roughly 20 business day Trading Windows, valid for only 5 business days, subject to the front page test whose refusal is final and confidential, and subject to the three-month short-term trading ban. Plan shares can never be hedged before vesting or while under a holding lock, so only fully vested unrestricted shares are candidates, and any price-triggered or conditional feature must be both placed and executed within a window. A collar could in principle be offered on an unsecured basis over vested unrestricted shares, and Directors, Employees and Contractors who are not Specified Persons are not caught by clauses 30 or 34 at all, but for the target population the funded structure is barred.

summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, subject to discretionary approval. Section 10 permits transactions that limit the economic risk of a Restricted Person's holding, and section 11 permits margin loans and other secured lending in relation to Company Securities, in each case only with prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer (the Chair for a director or KMP, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair, the Managing Director for nominated Employees). The structure must be confined to vested shares, because limiting the economic risk of unvested equity scheme entitlements is prohibited absolutely with no clearance route. Execution must fall outside the four Blackout Periods (half-year, annual and the March and September quarterly reports) and any confidential Board-imposed Additional Period, must not be done while holding Inside Information, and must be completed within the five business days for which clearance is valid unless the Approving Officer states a longer period. summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 11.1 prohibits Directors, KMP and Employees from trading in any financial products issued or created over the Company's securities, which captures both the purchased put and the written call whether traded OTC or on exchange, with no clearance route, no exceptional-circumstances relief and no distinction by vesting state. The section 10.1 hedging ban is narrower, reaching only arrangements that limit exposure to unvested or holding-locked securities, and the margin loan ban in section 11.1 is narrower still, reaching only borrowing used to finance the purchase of Company shares, so the secured loan leg over an existing vested holding is not itself expressly prohibited. That is of no assistance while the derivative overlay remains banned, and the policy is silent on encumbrances, margin calls and forced sales, giving a lender no comfort that enforcement during a Closed Period would be excused. summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, and this is one of the more permissive ASX policies for the purpose. There is no hedging prohibition at all: products that limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares are simply defined as SGH securities, so the put and call legs are dealings that a designated employee may execute inside one of the three 30-working-day window periods following the half year results, annual results and AGM, or outside a window with prior written clearance from the approver named in the section 3 table. Margin lending is likewise expressly permitted with written clearance, which may be granted subject to conditions, and a disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights is carved out of the policy entirely provided the facility itself was cleared, which protects the bank on enforcement. The two hard constraints are that no Executive or designated staff member may deal in any financial product issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities during a blackout period, with no exceptional circumstances relief, and that clearance lapses after two business days, so the trade must be fully documented before approval is sought. There is no ban on hedging unvested or restricted plan securities and no short-term trading or minimum holding rule, so vesting state and tenor are not obstacles.

summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable under this policy, which is markedly more permissive than most ASX policies on the financing leg. There is no prohibition on margin lending, secured financing, pledging or encumbering Lynas securities, granting security is not within the definition of Deal In Securities, and paragraph 8.1(6) expressly excludes from the policy a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights, so the bank's enforcement sale would not put the executive in breach even in a closed period. The derivative legs are the constraint: a put and call over Lynas shares are financial products created over the Company's securities and cannot be traded during prohibited periods (14.1), and since 7.3 makes every period a closed period except the three weeks following results, the AGM or a prospectus, entry, roll, unwind and settlement must each be timed into one of those narrow windows and preceded by written confirmation of no impediment from the Chairman (directors) or Secretary (employees). The 13.2 hedging ban reaches only employee options before vesting, so vested shares may be collared, but the undefined at all times ban on short-term trading in 13.1 argues for a long tenor and for clearing the structure explicitly. Out-of-window relief under 9.2 covers only a sale of securities, not derivative dealings, so no exceptional-circumstances route exists for an emergency unwind, and directors should expect the position to surface through immediate notification to the company secretary and an Appendix 3Y.

The financing legs are workable: a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement, a grant of security or rights over Xero Securities, and stock lending are all permitted with prior clearance under section 6, for Designated Persons and non-Designated Persons alike, with no restriction on using vested shares as collateral and no ongoing financier disclosure regime. summary: A funded collar is not available to a director or senior executive of Qantas under this Code. Nominated Qantas Employees (directors, company secretaries, direct reports to the CEO and their direct reports, and anyone else the CEO nominates) have their Dealing definition extended by paragraph 3.45 to catch both legs of the structure: hedging or any contract entered into to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to the Qantas share price, and any margin lending, securities lending or grant of charge, lien, pledge, right of set off or third party interest over Qantas Securities where control of the sale process may be lost. Both limbs are unqualified as to vesting state, apply equally to influenced family members and household associates, and there is no clearance path expressed for them; the only relief, paragraph 3.48, is granted by the Chairman or CEO in exceptional circumstances such as severe hardship or a court order, is valid for one month, cannot touch unvested Securities and on its face releases only the paragraph 3.44 prohibition rather than 3.45. Two features are worth testing with the Company Secretary: the drafting of 3.45 is ambiguous between an outright ban and an enlargement of Dealing that would make both legs available with a written Request to Deal outside the 30 June and 31 December Closed Periods, and the financing limb is qualified by 'where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost', which a structure giving the bank no independent power of sale may not trigger. There is no short-term dealing rule, no minimum shareholding requirement and no financier disclosure obligation, so tenor and reporting are not obstacles; ordinary Qantas Employees below the Nominated tier are subject only to the statutory insider trading prohibition.

The Policy does not ban secured financing or hedging outright: 'Other Designated Persons' may both limit the economic risk of their MinRes holding and use MinRes securities as security for loans, expressly including hedging and margin loan arrangements, provided prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer (Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair, Chair of the Board for other Directors, Managing Director for everyone else), and the excluded trading list then protects the bank's enforcement sale by carving out a disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights where that prior approval was obtained. summary: A funded collar is possible for an ALS director or executive over vested shares, and this policy is unusually accommodating on the derivative legs. Section 7 expressly permits the use of Derivatives, a term that names 'caps and collars' and 'any other hedging or investment arrangement' without venue limitation, in relation to vested Company Securities, while banning them outright over unvested equity incentives. The constraints are procedural and timing-based: Designated Personnel may only Trade in one of three one-month Approved Trading Periods following full year results, half year results and the AGM, a director must first inform the Chair and other Designated Personnel must obtain approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary, written confirmation goes to the Company Secretary within 2 business days, and the tenor must exceed six months to avoid the speculative trading ban on buying and selling within six months and on forward contracts. The loan leg is the live issue: there is no general prohibition on secured financing or on encumbering shares, but section 8 bans Designated Personnel from 'margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities', so the facility must be a fixed term loan without margin or top-up mechanics and should be confirmed in advance with the Company Secretary. The policy says nothing about forced sales, margin calls or lender enforcement, so any lender sale right should be exercisable only within an Approved Trading Period, and the Chair's exceptional-circumstances discretion covers sales only and would not authorise an out-of-window unwind.
